No web search, no standout source code, no other repositories. What I relied on
beyond docs/:

- General Rust/crate knowledge that is not standout-specific: clap 4 derive
  (`global = true`, `value_parser`, subcommand nesting, its exit status 2),
  serde, MiniJinja whitespace control (`{%- … -%}`) and `loop.last`, and
  serde_json's `preserve_order` feature plus cargo's feature unification — I
  added `serde_json = { features = ["preserve_order"] }` to `app/Cargo.toml`
  specifically so that the JSON standout emits carries my views' declared field
  order (`name`, `zone`, `machine_type`, `status`) rather than an alphabetical
  one. docs/ does not mention JSON key ordering either way.

- Black-box probing of my own built binary, where docs/ did not answer a
  question. Two answers came from probing rather than from a doc:
  (a) how to put a literal `[` in rendered output — I ran the binary with
  values `[compute]`, `[[compute]`, `\[compute]`, `[core/project]`, `[ compute]`
  and `[Compute]` and observed that `\[` is consumed as an escape while
  `[compute]` is treated as an unresolved tag;
  (b) that `Output::Artifact` with zero bytes and `allow_stdout()` really does
  leave stdout at 0 bytes while writing the report to stderr with exactly one
  trailing newline.
  Both are observations of the produced binary's behavior, not of standout's
  source.

answers.docs.gaps:
(a) Wrong. docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md, "Unknown Style Tags":

    | Output Mode | Behavior                    |
    | `Text`      | Tags stripped (plain text)  |

and docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md repeats it:

    | `Text` | Strip tags completely | Plain text, pipes, files |

What actually happened with `--output text` on a template containing an
undefined `[compute]`: the tag was **not** stripped — `[compute]` came through
as literal text — and a framework warning was emitted to stderr, "Unresolved
style tag(s) degraded to unstyled text: compute". The behavior is friendlier
than the docs claim, but the stderr warning is invisible in the docs, and for
an application whose contract pins stderr that difference is the whole ball
game.

(b) Missing. No page documents how to emit a literal `[` from a template.
`\[` works (and suppresses the warning); docs/ never mentions it. The nearest
thing is docs/crates/render/topics/template-engines.md's table of *MiniJinja*
delimiter escapes ("Escaped braces: `{{` renders as `{`"), which is pass 1 and
does not help with pass 2's BBParser.

(c) Missing. `Artifact`'s builder is named only in prose —
docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md shows
`Artifact::new(export.csv).suggest_destination(…).with_report(…)` and mentions
"stdout, if the application opted in with `allow_stdout()`" in the destination
policy — but there is no signature list, and nothing says whether an empty byte
vector is legal (it is), or whether the report is written with a trailing
newline (it is: exactly one).

(d) Missing. Nothing states how structured modes order object keys.
`--output json` sorts keys alphabetically by default, so a view declared
`name, zone, machine_type, status` serializes as `machine_type, name, status,
zone`. That is serde_json's default `Map`, and it is fixable only from the
application's own `Cargo.toml`, which is a surprising place to have to reach.

(e) Missing. docs/topics/output-modes.md says of `--output`: "The flag is
global—it applies to all subcommands", but nothing says whether a global flag
declared by the *application* is readable from the deepest `ArgMatches` that
`#[flag]` reads. It is (`#[flag] quiet: bool` works on a nested `config set`),
but I only learned that by running it.
answers.friction:
(a) Literal square brackets in output. `config list` must print `[core]` and
the three notices must print `[core/project]`, `[staging]`, `[prod]`. My first
attempt printed the section name plainly and the run said, on stderr:

    Standout :: Warnings
      Unresolved style tag(s) degraded to unstyled text: compute, core

That warning alone breaks SPEC.md's "Every other command that exits 0 leaves
stderr empty", so it had to go. Nothing in docs/ documents an escape; I found
`\[` by probing. Note `[core/project]` needs no escape (the `/` disqualifies it
as a tag) but `[staging]` does, so the templates escape uniformly.

(b) There is no documented channel for a success notice on stderr, and
docs/topics/error-handling.md is explicit that a handler must not write one
itself: "Do not print or call `process::exit` from handlers. This keeps capture
APIs, `TestHarness`, output ownership, and real process behavior on the same
seam." The only stderr-on-success row in the framework is in
docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md:

    | Artifact written to stdout | bytes to stdout, report to stderr | `0` |

so I reached for `Output::Artifact` with an empty byte vector — see the
workarounds answer.

(c) `--format` and `--output` both had to exist, with `--format` deciding.
docs/topics/app-configuration.md offers only rename or removal:

    .output_flag(Some("format"))  // --format instead of --output
    .no_output_flag()  // Disable entirely

Neither expresses "two flags, one of them wins", and
docs/topics/output-modes.md is equally firm that a handler must not see the
mode: "Output mode is a rendering concern and is deliberately absent from
`CommandContext`." So the reconciliation had to happen before `app.run`, on
argv.

(d) docs/topics/app-configuration.md leaves open which `ArgMatches` a
pre-dispatch hook gets:

    > Stating a single ordering rule for pre-dispatch hooks — including which
    > matches they receive — is issue #352 in the adopter-seams epic.

Since my hook reads the four global options, I wrote `global_value` to check
the matches it is handed and then walk down the subcommand chain, so it is
correct under either answer.

(e) `AppBuilder` has no "hooks for every command" seam, so the same
`Hooks::new().pre_dispatch(open_session)` is registered eight times, once per
path, from a `COMMAND_PATHS` constant. Minor, but it means adding a command
means remembering to add its path.

Nothing else fought back. The trailing-newline contract in
docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md ("The engine consumes exactly one final
newline" / "the process edge appends exactly one newline") was precise enough
that every template's byte-exact output was right the first time, and the
`ExternalFailure` description in docs/topics/error-handling.md ("Standout adds
no `Error:` prefix and no trailing newline") matched the binary exactly.

answers.summary:
`gcloudlike`, complete and working, in `app/`. `cargo build` and `cargo build
--release` are clean (the only warning is the sandbox's own `xcrun` cache
error, not the crate's).

Layout: `src/inventory.rs` (the three frozen rows), `src/settings.rs` (property
keys, INI set files, the configuration directory, and both resolution chains —
CLI-free, with 8 unit tests), `src/views.rs` (serializable view DTOs),
`src/handlers.rs` (`#[handler]` adapters), `src/main.rs` (clap surface,
`#[derive(Dispatch)]` command tree, `AppBuilder` wiring, 4 unit tests),
`src/templates/**` (8 MiniJinja templates, one per command path) and
`src/styles/default.css`.

Resolution happens once per invocation in a pre-dispatch hook registered on all
eight command paths; it builds a `Session` into `ctx.extensions`, so handlers
just read it. The two chains are kept separate in `Session::resolve`, and only
the active set's file is ever read, so nothing merges. Domain errors travel as
`ExternalFailure(1, "gcloudlike: …\n")`, which is what keeps the stderr payload
verbatim and the status at 1; usage errors (including malformed property keys,
which a clap `value_parser` rejects) stay clap's, at status 2.

Verified black-box against the produced binary with `check.sh` at the workspace
root: 89 assertions over argv → stdout/stderr/exit status, covering the
inventory, both chains and every precedence pair the spec names, set isolation,
the `active_config` file, INI parsing and the byte-preserving write, all five
domain errors, all seven usage errors, both forms and their conflict rule, and
`--quiet`. All 89 pass against both the debug and the release binary
(`pass=89 fail=0`), plus `cargo test` 12/12.
answers.workarounds:
Four, all in the CLI layer, all commented at their site:

(a) `reconcile_output` in `src/main.rs` rewrites argv before `app.run`. When
`--format json` is present it drops any `--output …` token and appends
`--output=json`; when `--format text` meets a structured `--output` it appends
`--output=text`. Any other line is passed through untouched, so the risk is
confined to lines that actually name both forms. `--format` is a real clap
flag (so `--format xml` is a proper usage error) and `--output` stays
standout's own. Four unit tests pin the rewrite, including that
`--output-file-path` is not mistaken for `--output`.

(b) `config set`, `configurations create` and `configurations activate` return
`Output::Artifact(Artifact::new(Vec::new()).allow_stdout().with_report(…))`.
There are no artifact bytes; the empty vector exists only to select the
"artifact to stdout" destination, whose documented report channel is stderr.
The effect is exactly right — stdout 0 bytes, stderr the rendered notice plus
one newline, exit 0 — and the notice's wording stays in a template rather than
in a handler, but the shape is being used for something it was not designed
for. Under `--quiet` these return `Output::Silent` instead.

One consequence I chose to accept rather than paper over: because the report is
rendered through the selected mode, `config set --format json` writes the
`{report, receipt}` envelope as JSON to stderr instead of the text notice.
Stdout is empty either way, and SPEC.md leaves these three commands' JSON open
("whatever JSON carries the content of their text form"), so I preferred this
to sniffing the command path out of argv in order to force the notice back to
text — that sniffing would have put the well-specified `--format json` cases at
risk to fix an unspecified one.

(c) The templates escape literal `[` as `\[` (`config/list.jinja` and the three
notice templates). This depends on an escape docs/ does not document.

(d) `app/Cargo.toml` declares `serde_json` with `preserve_order` purely so that
cargo's feature unification changes how *standout* serializes, giving the
machine projection the field order SPEC.md writes. The crate is never named in
the source. It is a lever pulled at a distance, so it is commented in the
manifest.

Also worth naming, though it is a judgement call rather than a workaround: the
active set is resolved and checked for existence on every command, including
`configurations activate`. That follows "Naming a set that does not exist is a
domain error, whichever source named it", but it does mean a hand-edited
`active_config` naming a deleted set cannot be repaired with `activate` alone.
